_comment: klt erc supply spec for the rcosc_top merged GDS -- the structural
power-delivery evidence T1 item 11 grades for an analog / custom block
(issue #37; klayout-tools design-evidence-tiers item text: 'klt erc
supply spec reports one island per supply and zero missing_tie; LVS
reference includes the supply nets (already true for SPICE references)').
Run it against the committed top-level layout:
klt erc layout/cells/rcosc_top.gds layout/erc-supply-spec.json \
--format json > layout/reports/rcosc_top.erc.json
No --top (the stream has exactly one top cell, rcosc_top -- the four
sub-cells are instantiated GDS sub-cells, not sibling tops) and no --pdk
(klt erc's antenna-ratio table today covers sky130 only; every antenna
verdict therefore reads 'unchecked', which item 11 does not grade).
layout/run_checks.sh runs this exact command and asserts the supply
conditions below.
GDS layer numbers are gf180mcu's own drawn-layer numbers, derived from
the PDK's own libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp (COMP 22/0, Poly2 30/0,
Contact 33/0, Metal1 34/0, Via1 35/0, Metal2 36/0, Metal2_Label 36/10,
Via2 38/0, Metal3 42/0, Via3 40/0, Metal4 46/0, Via4 41/0, Metal5 81/0,
Metal5_Label 81/10 -- all verified present with those numbers) AND
cross-checked against klayout-tools' curated gf180mcu deck layer table
(klayout_tools/decks/gf180mcu.py: metals, vias, and metal_labels, whose
per-metal pin/label purpose is datatype 10) -- not copied from another
PDK's spec.
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- stackup[0] MUST carry "role": "gate" (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at Poly2 rather than at Metal1. "active_layer": Comp
(22/0) makes the gate antenna denominator poly n diff instead of raw
poly area, which keeps THIS block's own poly-resistor bodies -- real
poly with no gate oxide -- out of gates[] entirely (klayout-tools
docs/cli/erc.md, 'Gate area'); without it every one of the 13 drawn
resistors would report a fictional antenna ratio
- Metal1/Metal2 carry the whole intra-block distribution: device
source/drain/tab metal inside the four sub-cells, the channel
router's metal1 columns, and its metal2 tracks between blocks.
Measured per-supply island composition on the committed GDS:
vdd = Metal1 71.8um2 + Metal2 101.3um2 + Metal3 307.7um2;
vss = Metal1 101.0um2 + Metal2 132.7um2 + Metal3 179.8um2
+ Metal4 264.0um2 (the CTIMING MiM bottom plate, which XCTIMING wires
to vss -- so vss genuinely routes through Metal4 and Metal4 cannot be
left out of the stack)
- "label_layer": "36/10" on Metal2 ONLY: that is the one layer this
block's merged GDS actually puts supply text on. Verified against the
committed GDS itself, not assumed from the standard-cell flow: every
pin label of rcosc_top (vdd, vss, clk, t0..t7) is on 36/10, there is
no 34/10 Metal1 pin text and no 81/10 Metal5 pin text in the stream
(this block is not a place-and-route standard-cell flattening, so the
worked example's 34/10 + 81/10 text layers do not apply). Declaring a
"label_layer" that carries no text would add nothing
- Metal5 and Via4 are deliberately NOT in this spec: the only Metal5 /
Via4 geometry in this GDS is the CTIMING top-plate jumper (gen_lib.py
add_mim_cap), which lands on vc, not on either supply. Declaring
Via4 would connect vss's Metal4 bottom plate to vc's top wire in the
2D connectivity model -- a conduction path the MiM dielectric in fact
blocks. Same device-vs-wire class as the Contact omission below
- There is deliberately NO Contact (33/0) via entry connecting Poly2 to
Metal1, and that is a recorded model gap, not an oversight: this
block's bias generator is a drawn-poly resistor ladder straight
across the rails (XRBA vdd-vh, XRBB vh-vl, XRBC vl-vss, plus XRBIAS
vdd-ibias), and the trim bank is a second ladder (XRFIX p-c1 .. XR7
c8-m, p = vdd). klt erc registers no device recognition at all
(docs/cli/erc.md, 'Connectivity model'), so with Contact declared
those resistor bodies conduct the two supplies into one electrical
island and report a FALSE erc.supply_short -- measured on this GDS:
full stack = 1 erc.supply_short naming vdd+vss; Contact omitted =
vdd one island, vss one island, distinct islands, zero supply
findings. Filed upstream as klayout-tools#2183 (whose sibling issues
#2180 and #2169 are the too-little / ties[]-collapse variants).
Omitting the poly-to-metal via is what keeps the supply-island
verdict about the metal power delivery -- the structural question
item 11 grades -- and leaves device-level connectivity to item 4's
own full-connectivity LVS, where this block already matches with
VDD/VSS pin correspondences at status "match". The known cost,
disclosed rather than hidden: every real transistor gate loses its
only path to metal in the connectivity model and is reported as an
erc.floating_gate finding -- 32 of them in the committed report --
which item 11 explicitly does not grade ('an antenna verdict or a
floating-gate finding in the same report ... is not this item's
subject and does not block it', klayout-tools#1994)
- "nets[]": vdd and vss, both "kind": "supply", which is what makes a
short between them report as the severe erc.supply_short rather than
the general erc.multiply_driven_net. Each must resolve to exactly
ONE electrical island: erc.unconnected_net fires on zero matches
AND on more than one, so zero findings of that rule plus zero
erc.supply_short naming either supply IS the 'one island per
supply' verdict, not merely an absence
- There is deliberately NO "ties[]" section here, and that is the
recorded blocker of issue #37 rather than an oversight: declaring
one on a real routed layout collapses this design into one
electrical island and reports a FALSE erc.supply_short
(klayout-tools#2169, reproduced four ways in gf180-drone-fc's
FRICTION F-034). Because "ties[]" is omitted, erc.missing_tie is
NOT COMPUTED by this run (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md: 'Omitted
entirely -> erc.missing_tie is never computed') -- its absence from
the committed report is an absence of evidence, not evidence of
absence. The well-tie evidence that DOES stand in for it:
(a) item 4's own LVS report layout/reports/rcosc_top.lvs.json carries
VDD and VSS as pin correspondences at status "match" -- the analog
branch of item 11 explicitly leans on this; (b) the merged GDS's own
PG pin labels vdd/vss on 36/10, which is what this spec's nets[]
entries match against; (c) rcosc_comparator's drawn shared n-well
group with its well_island tap on vdd (gen_lib.py draw_nwell /
klt gen well_island), documented in layout/README.md. The gf180mcu
deck's own body handling is a caveat, not evidence: it has no
distinct substrate-tap layer, so klt extract synthesizes a vsubs
body net for every NMOS and resistor rather than verifying drawn
taps (structurally unverified, per the deck's own _body_net_warnings)
-- which is exactly why no erc.missing_tie number is claimed here
